target_customer: Romantic couples, especially long distance, using a private messaging app
problem: General messaging apps mix partners with everyone else, so couples wanted a private shared space for messages, photos and moments.
business_model: Free consumer app; monetization not established in sources found

founders.name: Oleg Kostour
founders.background_notes: Named CEO of TenthBit by TechCrunch; YC bio says he co-founded a company acquired by Dropbox.

founders.name: Anton Krutiansky
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and by TechCrunch.

founders.name: Michael Petrov
founders.background_notes: YC bio: worked on iOS at Dropbox.

founders.name: Aswinkumar Rajendiran
founders.background_notes: YC bio: later CEO of Maple, earlier employee number 1 at Rippling.

founders.name: Jamie Murai
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page; named by TechCrunch as co-founder.

exit.reason: Wikipedia reports acquisition by Life360 on 2016-02-12 and the app defunct since 2019-04-22.

competitors.funding_then: Backed by Baseline, General Catalyst and Lightspeed

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile messaging and sharing app for two users on iOS and Android, straightforward for experienced mobile engineers.

defensibility.rationale: Shared history between a couple created some lock-in, but several rivals offered near identical features and network effects were limited to pairs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large messengers did not copy the couple-only model during the period found; competition came from other couple apps and the company merged with UK rival Cupple in February 2013.

market_need_then: The founders built it after being apart from partners during YC, and the VentureBeat 2012 numbers piece described couples messaging apps as hot at the time.

branding.name_origin: Renamed from Pair to Couple in February 2013 after TenthBit bought UK rival Cupple (VentureBeat).

identity.voice_and_tone: Romantic and playful; Pair was known for a thumb kiss feature (VentureBeat).

rebrands.why: Merged with the UK app Cupple and adopted the combined name.

branding.community_and_virality: Adweek, ABC7 and The Next Web covered the app; TNW reported 1 million users at its one year anniversary in March 2013.

brand_strength.rationale: Press coverage across several outlets and a memorable feature, but the plain real word name was generic and rivals had similar names.

pivots.why: Acquired UK rival Cupple and combined the apps.

outcome_analysis: Couple, first launched as Pair in March 2012, raised a 4.2 million dollar seed from a long list of angels and funds while in YC and grew to over a million users by March 2013 after merging with Cupple. The audience was limited to romantic pairs and no revenue model is documented, and Wikipedia reports it was sold to Life360 in 2016 and shut in 2019. The reasons for the later decline are not stated in the sources found, so the failure factors are inferred from the narrow market and absence of a recorded business model.
notes: No company website was listed in the directory data, so there was no site to fetch. The YC bio says Kostour and Krutiansky also co-founded Pair (YC W12) which Dropbox acquired; Pair is the earlier name of this same company per TechCrunch and Wikipedia, so that line likely describes a Dropbox acquihire of a different team and is not recorded as a previous startup. The seed date is 2012 (ZoomInfo gives 2012-04-30, Seedtable 2012-05) and the exact date was not confirmed at the primary source. CB Insights counts 2 rounds totaling 4.2M but the second round was not identified. Investor list copied from the TechCrunch listing in search results, not independently opened. Confidence is high only because founders, competition and funding are all sourced. Exit conflict: the directory says Inactive; Wikipedia reports acquisition by Life360 in 2016 and shutdown in 2019, so exit is recorded as acquisition.
